key_idea: Lift Vishik's unstable 2D vortex into a very thin, very large-radius axisymmetric no-swirl vortex ring. At large radius the axisymmetric Euler equations formally reduce to 2D Euler. Then treat viscosity as a perturbation by scaling up the background, and build the nonlinear solution on the unstable manifold of the self-similar steady state.
reason: The strategy reads as inevitable once stated: non-uniqueness becomes instability of a forced self-similar profile, Navier–Stokes reduces to Euler by scaling, and 3D reduces to 2D through a large vortex ring. The vortex-ring lift is the striking idea. But the execution is a chain of three spectral-perturbation steps (truncation, axisymmetric lift, viscous perturbation) plus a contraction-mapping construction, each with its own resolvent-convergence bookkeeping, so it is a clever but layered technical proof rather than a book proof.
recognized: Albritton–Brué–Colombo, 'Non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the forced Navier–Stokes equations' (Annals of Math 2022)
